classification.difficultyReason: Find the angles using the isosceles triangle, apply the sine rule, then devise a distinct perpendicular construction and combine right-triangle lengths to obtain AB again.

content.prompt: Using the information in the diagram below find

spec.description: Isosceles triangle ADC with B between A and C and internal segment DB. Single perpendicular equality ticks mark AD and DC. The narrow 20-degree sector has an external label and curved leader.
spec.mathematics: AD=DC=40 cm; angle ADB=60 degrees; angle BDC=20 degrees; A, B and C are collinear in that order. Coordinates derive from the given equal sides and angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; no computed angles or lengths are shown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ADC&=60^\circ+20^\circ=80^\circ\\\angle DAC&=\frac{180^\circ-80^\circ}{2}=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $AD=DC$, the base angles of triangle $ADC$ are equal. As $B$ lies on $AC$, $\angle DAB=50^\circ$.

Using the angle sum of triangle $ADB$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle DBA&=180^\circ-60^\circ-50^\circ\\\angle DBA&=70^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the length of $AB$ (to the nearest centimetre) using two different methods.

answer.short:
$37\text{ cm}$

Use the sine rule in triangle $ADB$, or split it into right-angled triangles.
answer.worked:
Method 1: sine rule in triangle $ADB$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{\sin60^\circ}&=\frac{40}{\sin70^\circ}\\AB&=\frac{40\sin60^\circ}{\sin70^\circ}\\AB&\approx37\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Method 2: let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $AC$. In isosceles triangle $ADC$, $DH$ bisects the apex angle, so $\angle ADH=40^\circ$ and $\angle HDB=20^\circ$. The point $H$ lies between $A$ and $B$.
$$\begin{align*}AH&=40\sin40^\circ\\DH&=40\cos40^\circ\\HB&=40\cos40^\circ\tan20^\circ\\AB&=AH+HB\\AB&=40\sin40^\circ+40\cos40^\circ\tan20^\circ\\AB&\approx37\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Both methods give $AB=37\text{ cm}$ to the nearest centimetre.
